newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TELECOMS AUTHORITY BANS CALLBACK SERVICES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TELECOMS AUTHORITY BANS CALLBACK SERVICES.

text.p: The South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority(Satra) said on Tuesday it would ban telephone callback operations, effective September 1, and said operators and users could be fined up to 500,000 rand ($107,000) if they fail to comply.
Satra chairman Nape Maepa told a news conference the decision, the first by the independent authority established in February, was based on an interpretation of the law and public interest.

"Satra hereby rules that all callback operations, including their associated support activities, constitute an offence...Operators and customers are hereby duly warned to cease and desist from such unlawful activities," Maepa said.
Gianfranco Cicogna, chairman of the South African Callback Association, said the industry, dominated by 10 operators, was worth about 18 million rand per month.
"We are shocked that in the South Africa of today where everybody is consulted about everything, we were not even given a chance to make a presentation before this decision was made," he said.
Cicogna said callback operators accounted for less than six percent of international telephone traffic.
